subject: Sales discovery: Redwood integration recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Sales discovery: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please ping me if I missed anything.

Top pain points you shared:
- Search relevance dropping when documents scale past ~100k (embeddings drift / inconsistent reranking)
- High tail latency (p95/p99) on your chat UX when load spikes during support hours
- Cost concerns for per-call generation and embedding lookups at your query volumes

Goals you framed:
- Improve search relevance and reranking quality across fresher content
- Bring p95 generation latency under ~200ms for 95% of interactive traffic
- Lower per-query costs while keeping deterministic outputs for compliance-sensitive flows

Integration / product fit notes we discussed:
- SDK changes: minimal — client calls map to Redwood’s text/generate and embeddings endpoints. We support both synchronous and streaming responses; streaming is recommended for your chat UX.
- Function calling: use structured function-calls to extract entities/actions (we can provide JSON schema templates). Good fit for automating follow-up tasks from chat.
- Structured outputs: Redwood can validate and return JSON as a first-class response (helps avoid brittle parsing).
- Streaming: supports chunked partial tokens + final JSON payload — reduces perceived latency for users.
- Embeddings & reranking: recommend using our text-embedding-4-small for initial tests, then tuning/dimensionality and an ANN index for your 100k+ docs. We also support rerank-by-embedding + cross-encoder rerank for top-N refinement.

Technical asks / next steps:
1) Share a representative dataset (anonymized) or sample of ~5k docs so our SE team can run a quick relevance baseline.
2) SE deep dive: Vivek to run a 60–90 min technical session to go over SDK snippets, function-calling examples, and streaming behavior.
3) Mutual action plan / procurement: I attached a draft MAP and a short proposal with indicative pricing.

Attachments: redwood-integration-proposal.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

If that all tracks, I’ll coordinate Vivek + your engineering lead for next week. Thanks again — excited about the fit here.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sales discovery: Redwood integration recap & next steps — SE notes and pre-read

Hi Sarah / Tom / Marissa —

Thanks for the sample dataset offer — that will help. A few technical notes and a short pre-read so the SE session is focused: \

1) SDK / function-calling pattern (pseudo):
- Client sends prompt + function schema to our /v1/chat/completions endpoint
- Redwood returns streaming tokens and flags function-call with args (JSON)
- Client confirms function execution and can resume conversation with updated state

2) Streaming behavior:
- We stream partial tokens for UX while continuing to build the final JSON payload
- For your chat use-case, enable chunk_size=256 and aggressive prefix caching to keep latency low

3) Structured outputs example (JSON):
- We support strict JSON schema enforcement (schema mismatch returns structured error object) — great for downstream automation.

4) Embeddings / rerank suggestion:
- Start with text-embedding-4-small (768 dim) for fast experiments. If top-N precision is low, run cross-encoder refinement on top-50.
- For 100k docs, use an ANN index (HNSW) with dynamic recall tuning; we’ll provide batch embedding helpers and a streaming embed endpoint for near-real-time content.

5) Performance knobs to hit p95 <200ms:
- Dedicated serving pool with autoscale + warm KV cache
- Quantized model variant for generation-heavy flows; fall back to full-precision for high-accuracy cases

Pre-reads I attached: arch-diagram.png (high level), plus I’ll bring an SDK sample repo to the call. Could you confirm S3 path and whether the sample needs any special redaction? Also let me know if you prefer Docker-based local testbench or a quick hosted sandbox we can spin up.

Available for the SE deep-dive: Tue 9am PT works for me. I’ll send a calendar invite once Sarah confirms Tom.

Thanks — Vivek
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
